description: Discriminating cases for threshold-block average precision. `superseded` is the M8 v1 value, retained so the regression stays visible. `expected` matches sklearn.metrics.average_precision_score.

cases.name: partially tied block: the case that broke M8 v1
cases.why: Admitting the tied block whole gives precision 2/3 at full recall: 0.5*1 + 0.5*(2/3). Averaging over orderings inside the block credits the positive for sometimes landing first.

cases.name: the superseded value errs LOW here
cases.why: A tied block at the bottom holding both positives. The v1 error is not one-directional: here it returns a value 0.083 BELOW the standard, which is why it is a different quantity rather than a bounded approximation. Found by exhaustive search over all score/label assignments of length <= 6.

cases.name: fully tied: AP equals prevalence
cases.why: One threshold admits everything; precision is the prevalence and recall is 1. Both implementations agree here, which is why fully-tied baselines were unaffected by the correction.

cases.name: untied, interleaved
cases.why: With no ties every block has size one and the two definitions coincide.

cases.name: mixed tied block
cases.why: A three-row block holding one positive.
